statement.p: The functions f and g and their tangent lines at (4,0) are shown in the figure below.

image.shortdescription: Graph of two intersecting functions and their tangent lines at the point of intersection

description.p: Graphs of two functions, f and g, which intersect at the point (4,0), and each of their tangent lines at the point of intersection.
f is a concave down function with positive slope and g is a concave up function with negative slope.

statement.p: f is shown in blue, g in black, and the tangent line to f is y = 0.8 (x - 4), and is graphed in red, and the tangent line to g is y = -0.4 (x - 4), and is graphed in green.

solution.p: Observe that both f(4) and g(4) are zero. Also, f'(4)=0.8 and g'(4)=-0.4, so by l'Hopital's rule, \lim_{x\to 4} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)} = \frac{f'(4)}{g'(4)} = \frac{0.8}{-0.4} = -2.
